title: Desiring the Face of God and the Coming of the King
english: They want to make a child of you; but desires produce a child of the devil. Again, those having the same desires are one generation. It is thus also with: 'The generation of the upright shall be blessed' (Ps 112:3). Jacob was seeking the face of God. Everyone praying sincerely for the appearance of God prays to receive it, and this is to seek the face of God. The saints indeed send up a prayer saying: 'Let your face shine upon us and we shall be saved' (Ps 27:8).

And this is also possible because: we have received the inscription of the psalm 'into one of the Sabbaths', and we call the resurrection of the Savior 'the Lord's Day', sometimes as the eighth [day] and sometimes as the first of the week according to various thoughts. They 'seek the face' of the one about to arrive, having heard that 'bending the heavens, he shall descend' (Ps 18:13), because 'a Savior is coming' (Ps 98:1). For the heralds of the truth, those running ahead of the one arriving, hear: 'Say to the daughter of Zion: behold, a Savior is coming to you' (Zeph 3:14), and: 'Say to the cities of Judah: behold, our God comes with might' (Isa 60:1), to shake off evil, so that we may learn to strike down the adversaries, those working evil, 'the one working in the sons of disobedience' (Ps 2:9).

Finally, having enjoyed the economy—for 'still' 'it shall say of your word: I am present' (Ps 105:4)—immediately the ascent of the Savior is signified after the arrival; for the word says through the psalms: 'Lift up your gates, O rulers of yours' (Ps 24:7). Your rulers, lift up the gates. Or thus: your gates, O rulers, lift up, which you preside over, which you guard. 'And be lifted up, O eternal gates' (Ps 24:9). The word says 'and be lifted up', presenting the greatness of the one about to descend and enter through the gates. If you remain here, you will not be able to contain his ascent. To lift up and to lift up [further] can also mean to make them through the middle; for he who is the very distant King does not need an entrance. And again: 'And the King of glory shall enter' (Ps 24:10). The heralds, angels, [announce] the Savior.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
